service.description: The objects of a calendar for CalDAV: each event series (not cancelled) by its name (the davName a client stored it under, else workEffortId.ics) with an entity tag over the rows that make its iCalendar text (the event, its recurrence, parties, the user's reminders and its changed instances), its time span for a time-range query, and the calendar's ctag over them all. No access check: the callers check the calendar.

The user's tasks for CalDAV's Tasks collection: the WetTask work efforts the user's party is assigned to now, not cancelled, and completed or closed ones only for 30 days after they were completed, each named by its UID (universalId, else workEffortId) with .ics, an entity tag over the task and the user's assignment, and the collection's ctag. A protected task (People's offboarding, separation and grievance-linked tasks, ChecklistStep isProtected; IronStone People design §12, F22) is left out, so a phone never lists, reads or changes it. A template and a step of managed work (a maintenance work order's, or of a process whose policy guards execution) are left out too, and a managed root (a maintenance work order) is listed read only (readOnly): a PUT or DELETE of it is refused (403) before anything changes, and its status changes only through its own lifecycle (IronStone Maintenance design §13.3; impl-maintenance P3, F63).

What a projected collection's owner service answers (CalendarProjection.ownerServiceName), as the user: admitted, whether the user sees the collection at all; and without checkOnly its events from start to end (epoch millis; the owner's own window when none) as the ICalendar tool's event maps (uid, sequence, summary, status, allDay, start and end in millis, or startDate and endDate days for an all-day event, timeZone, lastModified). The owner decides what each user sees; the projection kind adds nothing to it.

A projected collection's objects (collectionId projected-{projectionId}, its CalendarProjection not disabled) for the user: its owner service's events (none when it does not admit the user), each named by its uid with an entity tag over it, and the collection's ctag; admitted false for a user the owner does not admit or an unknown projection. A failure of the owner is logged and answers nothing.

The CalDAV collections of the user: each calendar the user may view (not free/busy only), read only below edit permission and for a subscription, named with its owner when shared; and Tasks (collectionId tasks, VTODO); and each projected collection whose owner admits the user (projected-{projectionId}, VEVENT, read only; P12). With collectionId only that one.

The objects of a collection, by name (objectNameList) or all, with their iCalendar text (withData, written as CalDAV calendar objects: no METHOD, the user's reminders as alarms); a calendar query's component (componentType) and time range (start, end in epoch millis; a recurring series is always in range).

Store an object a CalDAV client wrote: a calendar's event series (edit permission, not a subscription calendar) through store#CalendarFeedEvents by its UID, the name kept as davName; or a task in Tasks (a new one made with create#SimpleTask assigned to the user). A task the user is assigned to changes through the task services, as on the screens: its name, description, priority, percent complete, start and due through TaskServices.update#Task, its status through set#TaskStatus along the task's status flow (get#TaskStatusFlow; Complete sets the resolution and the completion date), COMPLETED being Complete or Closed; a to-do reopened from Complete, Closed or Cancelled goes to the first open status the flow allows from there. A status move the flow has not is refused with status 409 and nothing changes. A new start or end of an event that holds a meeting room or equipment (a current booking) is checked first as a move on the screens is (EventServices.check#ResourceBookings with the new time and checkOnly): a clash with another booking of it is refused with 409 and nothing changes; once stored, a booking of a resource with approvers is asked again (check#ResourceBookings). ifMatch and ifNoneMatch are the client's preconditions; status is 412 when one fails, 403 for a calendar the user may not change, 400 for text that holds no event or to-do (or several UIDs). Another refusal of a service it calls is an error: the whole change rolls back and the DAV server answers by it (409, 403 for access).

A CalDAV client's delete: an event series of a calendar (edit permission) is cancelled with its changed instances, or only taken out of this calendar when it is in another; a task leaves the Tasks collection by the end of the user's assignment (the task stays for the others on it). status 412 when ifMatch fails, 404 when the name is not there, 403 when the calendar may not be changed.
